papers.title: Engineering the 5-Year Food Matrix: Microbiological Safety, Oxidative Stability, and Sensory Viability for Mars-Class Deep Space Missions
papers.abstract: Background: Long-duration spaceflight architectures, such as projected Mars missions, require life support regimens capable of sustaining crew health for 900+ days without resupply. Emerging approaches toward higher-density, lipid-rich nutritional systems (including ultra-low carbohydrate paradigms) may optimize metabolic efficiency and mitigate microgravity-induced insulin resistance [1]. However, the technological translation of this metabolic paradigm necessitates profound innovations in food safety engineering. Objective: This perspective article examines the critical food safety and shelf-life constraints inherent to high-protein, high-fat matrices in spaceflight environments, and theorizes engineering pathways to achieve a 5-year stability threshold. Methodology: This narrative perspective integrates recent findings from space microbiology, radiation food chemistry, and food preservation engineering to propose design targets for ultrastable, high-lipid food matrices. Results: Lipid-dense matrices are susceptible to oxidative rancidity that may be further accelerated by secondary neutron radiation under certain exposure conditions, generating cytotoxic aldehydes. Traditional microbiological safety margins (e.g., thermal processing, A w reduction) likely require reconsideration to address enhanced pathogen stress resistance under microgravity. We identify four candidate technologies-freeze-dried matrices, structured lipid bars, UHT lipoprotein emulsions, and biopreserved fermented products-as foundational for extended missions. Conclusion: The viability of metabolic optimization strategies in space depends fundamentally on food matrix engineering. Resolving the dual threats of radiation-induced rancidity and microbial virulence in a 5-year shelf-stable, palatable format represents a critical path forward for Martian colonization architectures.

papers.title: Proxy-Only Fog-Cloud Bidirectional Distillation for Privacy-Preserving, Deployable IoMT ECG Diagnosis under Cross-Site Heterogeneity
papers.abstract: This work presents a proxy-only fog-cloud bidirectional knowledge distillation framework for privacy-preserving cross-site ECG diagnosis in Internet-of-Medical-Things (IoMT) systems. To satisfy data-governance constraints, hospital fog nodes and a cloud teacher collaborate solely via logits exchange on a public proxy dataset, avoiding patient data, labels, and model parameters. The proposed method stabilizes learning under cross-site heterogeneity and label shift while reducing communication overhead. Experiments on multi-site ECG data achieve 98.1% accuracy. An edge-oriented quantized FPGA deployment (1.98 ms latency and 0.169 mJ per inference) further demonstrates low-latency and energy-efficient real-time inference.

papers.title: Minimizing Data Collection Time for Passive BCI-based Assessment of Congenital Vision Deficiencies
papers.abstract: Objective: Brain-computer interface (BCI)-based color vision (CV) assessment is a new passive, objective, precise, and automatic method for identifying people with congenital redgreen CV deficiencies. At present, BCI-based CV assessment has limited practical utility because it requires lengthy data collection sessions. Here, we demonstrate a 97.5% reduction in the time required to perform BCI-based CV assessment, enabling identification of people with congenital red-green CV deficiencies in less than one minute with >99% accuracy. Methods: Previously collected BCI-based CV assessment data from 31 participants (20 controls, 6 protans, 5 deutans) were analyzed. Each participant completed four experimental runs sampling a 10×10 two-dimensional color grid of red-green intensity combinations around a yellow reference. Each grid location corresponded to a 3.75-s epoch of electroencephalography (EEG) recorded during alternation of the yellow source and the red-green mixture, resulting in 100 epochs per run (1500 s total). Baseline EEG was recorded before and after each run (60 s total), and 120-s breaks were provided between runs. A total 1920 s per participant. Results: Classification accuracies exceeding 99% were achieved using 2 runs of data from 5 grid locations. These locations correspond to regions previously identified in our prior work as showing the strongest inter-group differences. Conclusion: Our feature selection method reduced the time required for passive BCI-based CV assessment by 97.7% (i.e., from 1920 s to 45 s). Significance: The optimized BCI-based assessment accurately identifies people with red-green CV deficiencies in under one minute, greatly enhancing its clinical utility.

papers.title: Echinacea purpurea to treat Novel Coronavirus (2019-nCoV)
papers.abstract: Novel Coronavirus (2019-nCoV) or Human Coronavirus (HCoV) could be a new coronavirus that belongs to Betacoronaviruses type Human Coronaviruses, just like the Middle-East Respiratory Syndrome (MERS) coronavirus and Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome (SARS) coronavirus. Wuhan, the capital city of Hubei province, China recorded the initial cases of this virus in December 2019. Until 2 May 2020, 10:00 CET, near 23,8287 deaths were reported out of 3.34 million confirmed cases recorded across the world. By the tip of January 2020, China confirmed that the COVID-19 transmitted from human to human. This study aims to check a completely unique medicament called “Echinacea purpurea” against the crystal structure of 2019-nCoV Main Protease. This study presents an ideal model for Echinacea purpurea to be tested in silico against 2019-nCoV Main Protease.
